written_by: hand, from the boundary rules in `spec`; never produced by running ltcore.boundaries or tools/gen_fixtures.py
spec: A door is listed per page in page order. On one page a door without an item sorts first, then items by item_id as plain strings ('p3-12' < 'p3-21' < 'p3-9').

A report page is a door of class report-page (severity never-navigate). A checkpoint page (is_checkpoint) is a door of class checkpoint-page (severity stop). The only stop-severity class is checkpoint-page, so first_stop is the first live checkpoint page, else null.

An item with attempts single is a door of class single-attempt-item (severity per-item) unless it is submitted (read_only true and answered true) and its page is a single-pass page; then it is listed in single_attempts_passed instead. An item of type unmapped is a door of class unmapped (severity per-item).
The lock cause is lesson.run_locked true, else a checkpoints entry that is committed and not in_flow. With no cause there is no reach and no single-pass page.

Lock evidence is a top-level item (no parent_item_id) that is not a subpage, not unmapped, not a notebook, not a submitted single, not a mirror and not a permanent degrade. A page is locked when it has evidence and every evidence item has read_only true.

Under run_locked the reach is every non-report page, and every page of the reach is a single-pass page. Otherwise the reach runs from the first page up to, not including, the first page that has evidence and is not locked, or the first rat_candidate page that follows a locked page; the single-pass pages are the locked pages inside the reach; with no locked page inside the reach there is no reach.

inferred_locks lists each subpage child (parent_item_id set) with read_only null on a page inside the reach: class read-only-inferred when the page is locked, lock-unknown when the page has no evidence item, and nothing when the page has evidence that is not all true.
checkpoints_passed lists the index of every checkpoints entry that is committed and not in_flow.

c1-r101.why: Locked and completed run. run_locked makes every page of the reach a single-pass page, so both submitted single-attempt items are passed, not doors.

c1-r102.why: Writable run. The unsubmitted single-attempt item p3-21 and the unmapped item p3-23 are per-item doors; nothing stops the run.

c1-r103.why: No completion page. The single-attempt drag item p4-31 is a per-item door.

c1-r104.why: Committed checkpoint 8 left the flow, so it is the lock cause. Pages 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are locked; page 9 has writable evidence and ends the reach. p3-12 is submitted on locked page 3, so it is passed. Page 4 has locked evidence, so its children are read-only-inferred; page 6 has no evidence, so its children are lock-unknown.

c1-r105.why: Mirrors are not doors. Only the report page is listed.

c1-r106.why: Page 3 is a live, uncommitted checkpoint: the only stop-severity door, and no report page is captured behind it.

c1-r107.why: The notebook p1-16 has type unmapped, so it is a per-item door. The subpage child and the three multiple-choice items are not doors.

variants.why: The state before the user committed: no committed checkpoint, a live one before the team test, p3-12 still open. The single-attempt item is a door on page 3, the checkpoint stops the run at page 9.
A committed checkpoint out of the flow still causes the lock while a second, live one stops the run before the team test.
run_locked makes the whole run the reach, including the page with writable items; the lock evidence per page is unchanged.
No lock cause: a submitted single-attempt item alone proves nothing about its Submit control, so p3-12 stays a door.
Submission needs both answered and read_only evidence. The unanswered item remains a door; page 3 retains locked evidence, so its child locks remain inferred.
read_only null on p3-12 makes it evidence that is not true, so page 3 is not locked, the reach ends at page 3 and no page is locked inside it: no reach at all.
A writable single-attempt item on page 3 ends the reach there, so no page is locked inside it.
answered null is no evidence of a Submit, so p3-12 is a door; page 3 stays locked.
Doors on one page sort by item_id as plain strings: p3-12, p3-21, p3-23, p3-9.
A live checkpoint inserted before page 3 stops the run there; the per-item doors move to page 4.
Without run_locked and with no committed checkpoint there is no lock cause, so the submitted single-attempt items are doors again.
run_locked covers every page of the run, so a writable item on page 4 does not take p4-32 out of the passed list.
Once committed, the checkpoint leaves the flow: no stop, no door, and the container still records it as passed.
With two live checkpoints the first stop is the earlier page.
